items.why: Team plan capped at 200 users instead of unlimited members; already recorded as cognition-2026w40.
Mid-tier loses integrations, client collaboration and AI features while seats go from 5 to 10 and price from $83 to $67; already recorded as bugherd-2026w40.
The NewsletterXP Course, included on Max and Enterprise only, was removed from the feature comparison table between the Sep 21 and Sep 28 captures.

record.short: The NewsletterXP Course row was removed from the feature comparison table; it had been included on the Max and Enterprise plans only.
record.headline: beehiiv dropped the NewsletterXP Course from its Max and Enterprise plans.
record.who: Customers on the Max and Enterprise plans who used the course as part of their plan.
record.read: A bundled education perk is being taken out of the top plans, which fits a trend of trimming extras that cost the company to maintain. Small on its own.
record.caveat: The change comes from a comparison-table row; it is not clear whether the course is still available elsewhere.

items.why: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash cache-input price cut 77% from $0.03 to $0.007 per 1M tokens; GLM-5.3 Fast was also added and six models retired, which are not priced changes to existing models.

record.short: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash cache-input price cut from $0.03 to $0.007 per 1M tokens; input $0.30 and output $1.20 unchanged.

items.why: New cap of 50 automations per base on every plan (seen in the day and week pages); already recorded as airtable-2026w40.

Build and Scale replaced by four Success Package tiers (No Success Package $0, Core $29, Pro $999 minimum, Premier custom), with Zero Data Retention folded into Core and Pro; the concurrency cut is already recorded as vapi-2026w39, this record covers the plan restructure.

record.short: Build and Scale were replaced by four Success Package tiers: No Success Package ($0), Core ($29/mo), Pro (10% of hosting fee, $999/mo min) and Premier (custom); Zero Data Retention, a $1,000/month add-on, now comes with Core and Pro.
record.headline: Vapi replaced its Build and Scale plans with four Success Package tiers, from $0 to custom, and made Zero Data Retention part of the paid tiers.
rows: No Success Package, Core, Pro, Premier
Zero Data Retention add-on, per month
Included free with Core and Pro
record.who: All Vapi customers; those on Build or Scale have to pick a Success Package.
record.read: Moving from two self-serve tiers to a ladder that starts free and charges a share of hosting spend at the top looks like a push to tie Vapi’s revenue to customers’ usage. Making a $1,000 add-on part of the paid tiers is a strong nudge to upgrade.
record.caveat: PricingSaaS does not list the old Build and Scale prices, so only the new tiers are shown with prices.

items.why: Qwen3.7-Max serverless inference up 25% ($2.00 → $2.50 input); already recorded as together-2026w39.
Shopify Plus payment-processing rates, previously described only as competitive, are now shown as numbers; prices shown for the first time.

Flex billing FAQ rewritten; commitment allocation wording narrowed from organizations or instances to Self-Managed instances, with no price or allowance numbers changed.
The only change on the page is the Pro card bullet changing from Faster builds to Flat Rate CDN; no prices or allowances are shown in the evidence, so it is treated as copy.

record.short: Qwen3.7-Max serverless inference rose from $1.25 input / $3.75 output to $2.00 input / $6.00 output per 1M tokens; cached input went from $0.13 to $0.25.
record.headline: Together AI raised the price of Qwen3.7-Max serverless inference by 60%, and added DeepSeek V4.1 Flash to its catalog.
record.who: Developers calling Qwen3.7-Max on Together’s serverless API.
record.read: Hosts are repricing popular open models upward when demand is high; the cached-input rate nearly doubled, which hits agent and long-context workloads hardest.

items.why: Pro split into Pro, Plus ($20/mo) and Max ($50/mo) with 500/3,000/7,500 AI credits, and the flat $8/month Advanced AI Add-on was removed.

record.short: Pro was split into Pro, Plus ($20/mo) and Max ($50/mo) with 500/3,000/7,500 AI credits, and the flat $8/month Advanced AI Add-on was removed.

items.why: deepseek-v4-flash and the vision-exp model were merged into one deepseek-flash (V4.1) at lower cache-hit, cache-miss and output prices; the saved text gives no before/after numbers and says V4 Pro pricing is unchanged.

record.short: deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp were merged into one deepseek-flash (V4.1) model at lower cache-hit, cache-miss and output prices; V4 Pro pricing is unchanged.

items.why: Canva Pro fell 20% from US$180/year to US$144/year, and Free AI allowance was cut from up to 200 Standard or 20 Premium uses to up to 20; the existing canva-2026w38 record covers only the Premium tools relabel.

record.short: Canva Pro dropped from US$180/year to US$144/year, while the Free plan’s AI allowance was cut from up to 200 Standard AI uses or 20 Premium AI uses to up to 20 Standard or Premium AI uses.
record.headline: Canva cut the yearly price of Pro by 20% and, in the same update, sharply reduced the AI uses included for free.
rows: up to 200 Standard AI uses or 20 Premium AI uses
up to 20 Standard or Premium AI uses
record.who: Pro subscribers (price) and people on Canva Free (AI allowance).
record.read: A cheaper Pro paired with a much smaller free AI allowance reads as a push to move free users to paid when they want AI features.
record.caveat: Prices are shown in US dollars per year; the price cut covers one person on Pro.

items.why: Twilio Video moved from $0.004 per participant per minute to 5,000 free hours, then $1 per active user hour or $150 per named user per month; this reverses the Aug 24 change in the other Twilio report, so the page may be flipping between models.

record.short: Twilio Video moved from $0.004 per participant per minute to 5,000 free hours, then $1 per active user hour or $150 per named user per month.

items.why: Free Suite ($0/user/month) was removed from the Small Business CRM suites; only Starter Suite and Pro Suite remain.

record.short: Free Suite ($0/user/month) was removed from the Small Business CRM suites; only Starter Suite and Pro Suite remain.
record.headline: Salesforce dropped the free CRM suite from its Small Business lineup, leaving Starter Suite and Pro Suite.
rows: Free Suite, per user per month
Free Suite, Starter Suite, Pro Suite
record.who: Small businesses looking at Salesforce’s entry CRM; people who would have started on the free suite.
record.read: Removing the free entry point makes a paid plan the cheapest way into Salesforce’s small-business CRM, a step away from the free-plan-as-funnel approach.
record.caveat: PricingSaaS does not say what happens to existing Free Suite users.

record.short: Modal’s region selection surcharge dropped from 1.5-1.75x to 1.15-1.75x base compute prices on Starter, Team and Enterprise.

items.why: An FAQ term was renamed from database host to billable host and re-defined as a database instance; no prices or allowances changed on the page.

Jira automation quota renamed from rule runs to automation steps with new caps: Free 100 → 150, Standard 1,700 flat → 400 per user, Premium 1,000 → 750 per user, Enterprise Unlimited → 1,000 per user.

record.short: Jira’s automation quota was renamed from rule runs to automation steps: Free 100 → 150 per subscription per month, Standard 1,700 flat → 400 per user, Premium 1,000 → 750 per user, Enterprise Unlimited → 1,000 per user.
record.headline: Atlassian renamed Jira’s automation quota from rule runs to automation steps and set new per-plan caps, including a first cap on Enterprise.
record.who: Jira Cloud customers on all plans that use automation; teams with few users on Standard and heavy users on Enterprise are affected most.
record.read: Moving from flat pools to per-user caps and ending unlimited on Enterprise ties automation volume to seat count, which is likely to push heavy automation users toward higher spend.
record.caveat: The saved text gives the old Premium value without a unit, so whether it was per user or per subscription is not stated.

items.why: The hidden Contact us price on the Enterprise plan, renamed Growth/Enterprise, was replaced with a visible starting price of $18/user/mo (annual); prices shown for the first time.
Vercel Connect renamed Token Requests: included quota cut from 5K to 500 requests/month and overage raised about 10x, plus a new Triggers meter.

record.short: Vercel Connect, renamed Token Requests, now includes 500 requests/month instead of 5K and charges $3.00 per 1,000 requests instead of $3 per 10K; a new Triggers meter adds 1,000 included, then $0.95 per 1,000.

items.why: Metronome Startup plan moved from a $100,000 included billing allotment (10M events) to $0.04 per 1K ingest events plus 0.8% of billing volume; the T600 card reader is hardware and was left out.

record.short: Metronome Startup plan moved from a $100,000 included billing allotment (10M usage events) to $0.04 per 1K ingest events plus 0.8% of billing volume.

items.why: Business split into a Standard seat ($20/mo annual, unchanged) and a new Premium seat ($100/mo annual, $125/mo monthly, 5x usage), and Business is capped at 200 employees.

record.short: Business now has a Standard seat ($20/mo annual) and a new Premium seat ($100/mo annual, $125/mo monthly) with 5x usage, and is capped at 200 employees.
record.headline: OpenAI split its Business plan into two seat types, adding a $100 Premium seat with 5x usage, and capped Business at 200 employees.
record.who: Business customers; companies above 200 employees can no longer use the plan.
record.read: A higher-priced seat for heavy users plus an employee cap pushes larger companies toward Enterprise and lets OpenAI charge power users more without raising the standard seat.
record.caveat: The saved text calls this the OpenAI API Business plan; Standard seat prices are described as unchanged.
